validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification. Real, correctly classified.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently across multiple, genuinely separate origins. Russian Wikipedia's dedicated article opens '«Прогресс» («Ямбург — западная граница СССР») — магистральный экспортный газопровод, построенный Советским Союзом в 1988 году' (a trunk export gas pipeline built by the USSR in 1988) and gives diameter 1400mm, working pressure 7.4 MPa, capacity 26 bcm/y. Ukrainian Wikipedia's separate article corroborates independently (1988, 1400mm, names the compressor-station chain from Yamburg through Ordynskaya to the Ukrainian border). Neftegaz.ru (Russian trade press, Nov 2020) reports a fire on 'магистральный газопровод Прогресс' in Yamalo-Nenets AO — an incident report naming the exact line, independent of any Wikipedia lineage. Ukraine's own gas-design institute YUZHNIIGIPROGAZ (ungg.org) lists 'Yamburg – Western Boarder (Progress)' among the trunk systems it engineered in the 1980s. gpf-europe.com's capacity table (European Geopolitical Forum, an independent geopolitics outlet) separately lists a 'Yamburg-Western border (Uzhgorod)' export line among Ukraine-transit pipelines. Five independent origins (2 language-Wikipedia articles, 1 Russian trade-press incident report, 1 Ukrainian design-institute history page, 1 geopolitics-outlet capacity table) is well past the 2-independent bar — this is not a GEM-only or hallucinated entity. CLASSIFICATION: every source calls it a 'магистральный' (trunk/main) gas pipeline — transmission is correct, not a gathering/feeder line. Naming also checks out: GEM's OtherLanguagePrimaryPipelineName 'Газопровод "Прогресс"' and OtherLanguageAlternativePipelineNames 'Ямбург — Западная граница СССР' match the sources' own naming exactly.

validity.recommendation: No merge. Do not fold into P0768 (Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod). Worth a one-line ResearcherNotes cross-reference since the two share a corridor for most of their route.
validity.researcher_notes: Checked directly against the obvious candidate on the roster, P0768 Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod ('UPU'), because both are Soviet 1980s Yamalo-Nenets-to-Uzhhorod export trunks feeding the same Bratstvo/Brotherhood system. They are NOT the same pipe: different origin fields (P0774 = Yamburg field; P0768 = Urengoy field, ~250km apart), different diameters as recorded (1400mm vs 1420/1400mm), different capacities (26 vs 32 bcm/y), different construction years (1988 vs 1983), and Ukrainian Wikipedia is explicit that they are two separate physical pipes that happen to run in the same bundled corridor: 'Прогрес' 'сходиться на КС Ординська в Центральний газотранспортний коридор' with Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod (converges into the shared corridor at Ordynskaya CS), and after Yelets/that point 'Прогрес прямує разом з Уренгой — Помари — Ужгород' (Progress proceeds together with UPU). This is standard Soviet megaproject practice: multiple independently-built, independently-operated parallel strings sharing one right-of-way/bundle for hundreds of km, not a single pipeline recorded twice. Several low-quality Russian SEO aggregator sites (fb.ru, in.minsk.by) recycle the same '1160 km through Ukraine' figure for BOTH Progress and UPU, which is exactly what you'd expect if they share the Ukrainian-territory corridor length — consistent with 'parallel, not identical' rather than evidence of a double-count.

validity.recommendation: Flag Capacity as needing a primary-source check (a TSOU technical/capacity document), rather than treat 26.00 bcm/y as fully settled. Do not change the value on this pass — the split evidence doesn't clearly favor one number.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Capacity=26.00 bcm/y is matched EXACTLY by Russian Wikipedia ('Его пропускная мощность составляет 26 млрд. кубометров природного газа в год'), which is a genuine 1-source-exact-match. But two other, differently-sourced pages give a materially different number for the same pipeline: English Wikipedia's 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' article states 28.5 bcm/y, and gpf-europe.com's (European Geopolitical Forum) FSU pipeline-capacity table lists 'Yamburg-Western border (Uzhgorod)' at 28 bcm/y. That's a real ~7-8% split across sources that don't obviously share one origin (an English-language Wikipedia editorial page vs. a specialist geopolitics-outlet capacity table vs. Russian Wikipedia), so per the 'material disagreement is never silently passed' rule I'm flagging it rather than treating the one exact match as dispositive. Plausible explanations I can't confirm: 26 vs 28 could be technical/design vs. de-rated/current-utilised capacity, or a Soviet-era nameplate figure vs. a post-Soviet re-rating — but I found no source that explains the discrepancy directly.

validity.recommendation: No change to LengthKnown=4590.70 km. Worth noting in ResearcherNotes that secondary Russian-language sources phrase the Russia/Ukraine split ambiguously (see notes) — a TSOU primary document would settle it cleanly if anyone wants to go further.
validity.researcher_notes: Length looked like a hard conflict at first read and I want to show the work rather than either rubber-stamp or over-claim a defect. Russian Wikipedia's sentence 'Протяжённость газопровода – 3473 км (1160 км по территории Украины)' reads, taken alone, as TOTAL length 3473 km, of which 1160 km is in Ukraine — which would conflict hard with GEM's 4590.70 km (~24% over). But Ukrainian Wikipedia's OWN separate article states explicitly 'протяжність якого територією Росії становить 3473 кілометри' — i.e. 3473 km is the length WITHIN RUSSIA specifically, not the total. That's a materially different claim using the identical number. Combining the two more precisely-worded figures I could find — 3473 km in Russia (uk.wikipedia, explicit) + ~1,120-1,160 km in Ukraine (en.wikipedia's Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine article gives 1,120 km for Progress's Ukrainian section specifically; ru.wikipedia/fb.ru's reused figure gives 1,160 km) — yields a total of roughly 4,593-4,633 km, which lands within about 1% of GEM's 4,590.70 km. I also checked GEM's own LengthEstimateKm field (4,536.71 km, presumably geometry-derived off the mapped RouteAccuracy=high route) purely as an internal consistency check (not cited as a source, per standing rule 1) — it's within ~1.2% of LengthKnown, which is additional (non-citable) reassurance the reported figure isn't wildly off from the actual mapped geometry. Net: I read this as reasonably corroborated within normal measurement variance, not a material disagreement with GEM — but flagging the ambiguous/contradictory phrasing in the two most convenient secondary sources so a future pass doesn't cite them as if they agree, and so a from-scratch TSOU primary check remains an open, cheap way to fully close this out.

validity.recommendation: No change. Owner/Operator split is defensible as recorded.
validity.researcher_notes: This IS a genuine cross-border pipeline (Yamburg, Russia -> Uzhhorod, Ukraine), so the country rule about Gazprom never owning Ukrainian assets applies to the UKRAINIAN section only, and GEM's record already reflects the split correctly: Operator = 'Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, Gazprom' and Owner1=Gazprom PJSC / Owner2=Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine, with NEITHER Owner1% nor Owner2% populated (checked the live operators/owners sheet directly, row 691: both blank) — i.e. the record does not assert Gazprom owns any percentage of the whole pipe, unlike a real defect I'd flag if it did (P0768's sibling row shows exactly that pattern with an unsupported 100.00% on Gazprom; P0774 does not have it). Ru.wikipedia's 'Газотранспортная система России' article independently confirms Gazprom operates almost all of Russia's trunk network and explicitly lists 'Прогресс' among Gazprom's pipelines, i.e. its role is scoped to the Russian segment, consistent with GEM. En.wikipedia's 'Natural gas transmission system of Ukraine' article confirms the Ukrainian system is 'owned by Government of Ukraine and operated by Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine' — a legal owner/operator distinction that GEM's own Parent field already captures correctly (Parent = 'Ministry of Energy (Ukraine) [unknown %]', not TSOU), so TSOU sitting on the Owner line is a reasonable simplification given GEM's layered Owner/Parent model, not an error. No Gazprom-owns-Ukraine-assets problem here.

validity.recommendation: Keep Status=operating. Add a ResearcherNotes line on the 2025-01-01 transit cessation for context; do not infer a status change from it.
validity.researcher_notes: This line's historically dominant function was Russian-transit export (it enters Ukraine via the Sudzha gas metering station per en.wikipedia — the same Sudzha crossing the country guidance identifies as the sole remaining transit entry point after Sokhranivka closed in 2022, and which stopped carrying Russian transit gas when the Gazprom-Naftogaz contract lapsed unrenewed on 2025-01-01). That cessation is real and specific to this corridor, not just a generic country-wide inference — but per the country guidance it is not grounds on its own to move Status off 'operating': Ukraine's GTS (of which this trunk's Ukrainian section is a physical part) continues in service for domestic transmission and reverse-flow imports, and I found no dated evidence the physical asset itself has been idled/decommissioned. Recommend documenting the transit-cessation fact in ResearcherNotes as a deliberate, sourced caveat.

summary: P0774 Progress Gas Pipeline: existence/classification/attribution/status all confirmed (caveat) across 5+ independent sources; NOT a duplicate of P0768 (UPU) despite sharing a corridor through Ukraine; length (4590.70km) confirmed-with-caveat via a Russia(3473km)+Ukraine(~1120-1160km) composite that lands within ~1% of GEM's figure once ambiguous secondary-source phrasing is untangled; capacity flagged as an unresolved spec concern (GEM/ru.wikipedia 26 bcm/y vs en.wikipedia/gpf-europe.com 28-28.5 bcm/y).
